stops.title: Progressive waves & reflection of waves
stops.inShort: A simple harmonic progressive wave is y = A sin(ωt − kx). On reflection from a denser medium, a transverse wave undergoes a phase change of π (crest becomes trough); from a rarer medium, phase change is 0.

stops.title: Superposition of waves & stationary waves
stops.inShort: Superposition: y = y₁ + y₂. Two identical progressive waves travelling in opposite directions interfere to form a stationary wave: y = 2A cos(kx) sin(ωt). Distance between two consecutive nodes (or antinodes) is λ/2; node to adjacent antinode is λ/4.
sections: 6.5.4 Comparison of Progressive and Stationary Waves

stops.title: Free, forced vibrations, harmonics & overtones
stops.inShort: The lowest natural frequency is the fundamental frequency (1st harmonic). Integral multiples of the fundamental are harmonics; frequencies actually present above the fundamental are overtones.

stops.title: Vibrations of air column in pipes & end correction
stops.inShort: Pipe closed at one end: only odd harmonics (n, 3n, 5n...), n = v/(4L). Pipe open at both ends: all harmonics (n, 2n, 3n...), n = v/(2L). End correction e = 0.3 d (or from two lengths).

stops.title: Vibrations of a stretched string & sonometer
stops.inShort: Fundamental frequency of stretched string: n = (1/2l) √(T/m). Laws of vibrating string: n ∝ 1/l, n ∝ √T, n ∝ 1/√m. Verified using a sonometer.

stops.title: Beats & characteristics of sound
stops.inShort: Beats are periodic waxing and waning of sound due to superposition of two waves of slightly different frequencies: beat frequency N = |n₁ − n₂|. Used in tuning instruments and Doppler radar.

items.s: Corrected length L = l + e (closed) and L = l + 2e (open).
m is linear mass density (mass per unit length).
Two successive maxima or minima are separated by T_beat.

board.text: A string of length 2 m is vibrating with 2 loops. The distance between its node and adjacent antinode is ____.
board.answer: (a) 0.5 m (2 loops = λ = 2 m, so node to adjacent antinode = λ/4 = 0.5 m).

Harmonics: Integral multiples of the fundamental frequency (n, 2n, 3n, ...) are called harmonics. The fundamental frequency is the first harmonic.
Overtones: The frequencies higher than the fundamental frequency which are actually present in a given sound are called overtones. The first higher frequency present is the first overtone.

board.text: Obtain an expression for practical determination of end correction: (i) for a pipe open at both ends and (ii) for a pipe closed at one end.
board.answer:
(i) Open pipe: v = 2 n₁ (l₁ + 2e) = 2 n₂ (l₂ + 2e) ⇒ n₁ l₁ + 2 n₁ e = n₂ l₂ + 2 n₂ e ⇒ e = (n₂ l₂ − n₁ l₁) / [2(n₁ − n₂)].
(ii) Closed pipe: v = 4 n₁ (l₁ + e) = 4 n₂ (l₂ + e) ⇒ n₁ l₁ + n₁ e = n₂ l₂ + n₂ e ⇒ e = (n₂ l₂ − n₁ l₁) / (n₁ − n₂).

points.text: End correction formula for open pipe: e = (n₂l₂ − n₁l₁)/[2(n₁ − n₂)]
End correction formula for closed pipe: e = (n₂l₂ − n₁l₁)/(n₁ − n₂)

board.text: Distinguish between free vibrations and forced vibrations (two points).
board.answer:
1. Free vibrations occur when a body is displaced and left to vibrate on its own without any external periodic force; forced vibrations occur under the action of an external periodic force.
2. Frequency of free vibrations is the natural frequency of the body; frequency of forced vibrations equals the frequency of the external periodic force.

board.text: Explain the analytical method to determine beat frequency.
board.answer:
Let two sound waves of equal amplitude A and slightly different frequencies n₁ and n₂ arrive at a point: y₁ = A sin(2π n₁ t), y₂ = A sin(2π n₂ t).
Resultant y = y₁ + y₂ = 2A cos[π(n₁ − n₂)t] sin[π(n₁ + n₂)t] = R sin[π(n₁ + n₂)t].
Intensity is maximum when R = ±2A, i.e. cos[π(n₁−n₂)t] = ±1 ⇒ π(n₁−n₂)t = 0, π, 2π...
Time between two consecutive maxima = 1/|n₁ − n₂|. Hence beat frequency N = |n₁ − n₂|.
